core_obligations: Recall the criterion (proof line 3077): by the definition of K-flatness it suffices to show that Tot(M^bullet tensor Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet)) is acyclic for every acyclic complex M^bullet.

Apply the associativity isomorphism (proof lines 3069-3076): the displayed canonical isomorphism rewrites that total complex as Tot(Tot(M^bullet tensor K^bullet) tensor L^bullet), moving the testing complex next to K^bullet.

Conclude (proof lines 3076-3077): since K^bullet is K-flat, Tot(M^bullet tensor K^bullet) is acyclic for acyclic M^bullet, and since L^bullet is K-flat the total tensor product of that acyclic complex with L^bullet is acyclic as well, which is what had to be shown.
proof_roadmap: Test K-flatness of the total tensor product against an arbitrary acyclic complex M^bullet.
Use associativity of the total tensor product to move M^bullet next to K^bullet.
Apply K-flatness of K^bullet and then K-flatness of L^bullet to keep acyclicity.
Conclude by the definition that the total tensor product is K-flat.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the total complex of the tensor product of two K-flat complexes is again K-flat (statement lines 3059-3066). The proof is a reduction organised by the associativity isomorphism for total complexes: testing against an acyclic complex M^bullet, the displayed canonical isomorphism Tot(M^bullet tensor Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet)) = Tot(Tot(M^bullet tensor K^bullet) tensor L^bullet) (proof lines 3069-3076) moves the test complex next to K^bullet, after which K-flatness of K^bullet makes the inner total complex acyclic and K-flatness of L^bullet makes the outer one acyclic, so the definition gives the conclusion. The content is the choice of the correct associativity isomorphism. The claim is H2: one displayed isomorphism plus two applications of the definition.
